study.title: Acupuncture for Migraine Without Aura and Connection-Based Efficacy Prediction: A Randomized Clinical Trial
study.randomization: Computer-generated code with fixed block size 4, performed by an independent statistician, via an interactive web-based system (Beijing LNKMED Tech Co Ltd)
study.blinding: Single-blinded; participants, outcome assessors, and statistical analysts were blinded to group assignments
study.population: Participants aged 18 to 65 years who met the MWOA criteria of the International Classification of Headache Disorders, 3rd edition
study.inclusion_criteria: Diagnosis of MWOA according to ICHD-3; age 18 to 65 years; 2 or more migraine attacks in the past 4 weeks; 1 year or longer migraine history
study.exclusion_criteria: Specific headache types per ICHD-3; use of migraine preventive treatment, acupuncture, or migraine devices within the past 3 months; history of medication overuse-related headache; serious medical conditions, pregnancy, lactation, or inadequate contraception; contraindications to MRI
study.source_location: Abstract, Methods: Trial Design and Participants, page 1-3

arms.dropouts: 1 discontinued treatment due to scheduling conflict at week 2; 1 refused MRI scan (excluded from neuroimaging)

5 discontinued treatment (2 pain and scheduling conflicts at weeks 2 and 4, respectively; 2 lack of efficacy at week 3; 1 dropped out at week 4); 3 excluded from MRI (2 refused, 1 did not complete due to noise); 4 excluded due to head motion

conditions.timepoint_exact: baseline (before treatment; at least 72 hours after a migraine attack, interictal phase)
conditions.source_location: Methods: Neuroimaging Acquisition and Network Construction, page 4

conditions.tissue_level_reasoning: Explicitly described as 'superficial needling' at a 'superficial' depth, indicating the needle enters the skin but only to a shallow cutaneous level (1-5mm), engaging cutaneous fibers only. Non-meridian sham acupoints and omission of deqi are consistent with this superficial insertion level.

interventions.anatomical_location_exact: Baihui (GV20), Fengfu (GV16), bilateral Fengchi (GB20), bilateral Taiyang (EX-HN5), bilateral Hegu (LI4)
interventions.laterality_exact: bilateral for Fengchi, Taiyang, Hegu; midline for Baihui and Fengfu
interventions.manipulation_exact: Twirling, lifting, and thrusting aimed to elicit deqi (distention, numbness, soreness, or radiating sensations)
interventions.deqi_intended_exact: yes; deqi sensation (distention, numbness, soreness, or radiating sensations) was intended
interventions.treatment_period_exact: 4 weeks (3 sessions per week, ideally every other weekday)
interventions.practitioner_description_exact: Acupuncturists had at least 5 years of clinical experience
interventions.participant_instructions_exact: Treatments were delivered individually, with standardized instructions for maintaining consistency
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: Acupoint prescriptions followed those used in prior studies

extraction_notes.note: Real acupoint locations (eFigure 1, eTable 1), acupoint manipulation details (eTable 2), and sham acupoint locations (eFigure 2, eTable 3) are in Supplement 3 only. Some sham acupoint anatomical details not reproducible from main text.
Baseline demographic and clinical characteristics tables (eTables 4 and 5) and per-protocol outcomes (eTable 6) are in Supplement 3. These are not extracted here.

Detailed satisfaction data (eTable 7), expectancy scale scores (eTable 8), compliance data (eTable 9), blinding assessment results (eTable 10), and adverse events by type (eTable 11) are in Supplement 3 only.

Figure 2B and Figure 3B show brain visualizations of robust network edges for VAS and HIT-6 CPM models respectively. Exact node coordinates for these edges are not provided in main text or tables; they appear only as brain images.

Figure 4 panels A and B show anatomical distribution of VAS and HIT-6 robust network nodes with circle size indicating node importance, but no MNI coordinates or quantitative node statistics are provided in the main text.

The n_analyzed for CPM analyses is stated as 59 for the real acupuncture group (those who completed baseline rs-fMRI scan). It is unclear from the main text whether the CPM was conducted only in the real acupuncture group or in both groups combined. The framing in the methods suggests CPM was applied to real acupuncture participants only, but this is not explicit.
extraction_notes.source_location: Methods: CPM of Clinical Outcome, page 5; Figure 1, page 3

extraction_notes.note: The CPM analysis for sham group is not mentioned separately. It is ambiguous whether CPM was run on sham group participants, or only on real acupuncture participants. The n_analyzed for CPM is inferred to be 59 (real acupuncture completers with valid scans) based on Figure 1.
extraction_notes.source_location: Figure 1, page 3; Methods: CPM of Clinical Outcome, page 5

extraction_notes.note: No quantitative deqi ratings (e.g., MASS, SASI, or similar instruments) were reported for either arm. The paper only states deqi was intended for real acupuncture and omitted for sham acupuncture.
No post-treatment fMRI data were collected. The paper acknowledges this as a limitation and states future studies should include posttreatment MRI data.
Coordinate space (MNI or Talairach) for the CPM network nodes is not explicitly stated in the main text.
extraction_notes.source_location: Methods: Neuroimaging Acquisition and Network Construction, page 4-5

extraction_notes.note: No actual MNI or Talairach coordinates for any brain region are reported in the main text. All nodal anatomical descriptions are narrative (e.g., 'limbic system, prefrontal cortex, putamen, and occipital lobe').
